[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Factions[/color][/head]
Crescent's wars overlap rather than dividing into neat teams. These are the major powers and the interests that keep each one in Taypan.
The selected [textlink="Gamemode" link="Gamemodes"] decides which factions are available. For a first round, choose DSM or NCWL; their entry roles have no playtime requirement.
[head=3][color=#684871]Divine Sol Mandate (DSM)[/color][/head]
The Mandate is a loose elective imperial order of noble territories, Crown domains, chartered cities, guild jurisdictions, and religious estates. Count Olywier Rabenau holds Crescent's principal Imperial charter. His government wants sovereignty, dues, strategic depth, and a frontier that remains recognizably Imperial.
The Lord Admiral commands Olywier's active frontier military. The Imperial Adjutant represents the Crown as an observer and diplomatic liaison, without routine local command authority. Noble, burgher, Saintsworn, Freeholder, and Oathbound interests all compete inside the same charter.
[color=#8fc98a]No minimum playtime. Recommended first job: Freeholder for humans, Oathbound for every other species. Ask on the Imperial civilian channel (:j) where you should report.[/color]
[head=3][color=#bf4d00]New Crescent Workers' League (NCWL)[/color][/head]
The NCWL is the provisional revolutionary front of the Crescent campaign, not a permanent sovereign country. It administers contested territory, coordinates fleets and militias, distributes supplies, and carries the Workers' Union project outward from secure Chengridz.
Player-led parties or coalitions select the League's field leadership, which Chengridz ratifies with Kane's approval. MVD officers remain Workers' Union political-security personnel rather than servants of the winning party. The Homeguard is the professional military inheritance of the first uprising.
[color=#8fc98a]No minimum playtime. Recommended first job: Union Worker; League roles are closed to Voidborn. Ask on :o which union, crew, or supervisor needs help.[/color]
[head=3][color=#535961]Shinohara Heavy Industries (SHI)[/color][/head]
Shinohara is the largest corporate power active in Crescent. It links drydocks, freight, finance, insurance, fabrication licenses, warehouses, cloning services, research, and armed security into one system. Its preferred victory is not annexation but dependency.
Prometheus Shipyards spreads SHI standards through the fleets it builds and repairs. Tatsumoto handles deals that let enemies remain customers. CorpSec prevents loss; Corporate Liquidation ends situations where prevention has failed. Every use of force is expected to have an accounting purpose.
[color=#d9b86c]Requires 3 hours and 1 completed round. Trade-heavy and high tech; learn the basic economy and ship systems first.[/color]
[head=3][color=#ff7f7f]Taypani Free Companies Federation (TFCF)[/color][/head]
The TFCF is a Taypani federation of four distinct organizations: Gorlex Security Consulting, Interdyne Pharmaceuticals, Cyberdawn Technologies, and the Shipbreaker Astronautics Workers Union. It is anti-Shinohara without being anti-capitalist; its members want an open market in which SHI cannot decide who is allowed to operate.
The four jointly choose an Administrator with final authority over Federation-wide war, diplomacy, common infrastructure, territorial claims, and major joint contracts. Each member retains its own leadership and culture. Competition is allowed; betrayal of a Federation commitment is not.
[color=#d9b86c]Requires 3 hours and 1 completed round. Choose a member company that matches your job and follow both its local supervisor and valid Federation commitments.[/color]
[head=3][color=#4f8b63]Taypani-Atyrian Pact (TAP)[/color][/head]
The Pact is a mobile confederation of four great family networks: Izdari traders, Arabet spiritual and psionic authorities, Al'Seik warriors, and Thukker engineers. Kinship can be created through blood, adoption, oath, marriage, or long service. The aging carrier-workshop Aasim is a famous common market and meeting place, not a fixed capital.
[color=#d9776c]Requires 10 hours and 3 completed rounds. This is an advanced, irregular faction and is not recommended for a first character.[/color]
[head=3][color=#b08a55]Gliess Santo and the Colonial Minutemen (CMM)[/color][/head]
Dockmaster Leo King's Articles make Gliess Santo a neutral port where outside warrants and wars do not automatically override station law. The Gliessian Sheriff and their deputies, who appear in the job list as Gliessian Militiamen, inherit the civilian-protection, public-accountability, and local-jurisdiction traditions of the Colonial Minutemen, whose headquarters Analiesse was destroyed after their break with the Mandate.
[color=#8fc98a]Gliess jobs appear in applicable presets. Gliessian Dockhand is the safest entry role; follow the Dockmaster and local station law.[/color]
[head=3][color=#8b1a1a]The Saint's Militia[/color][/head]
The Saint's Militia is one radical militant movement with four doctrinal currents: Serraine's Mercy Furnace, Romaine's Final Crusade, Remiel's Living Codex, and Guies's Divine Balance. It is not a separate Romaine faction. The movement hunts psions and targets communities it considers outside a purified human order, placing it in conflict even with Mandate authorities who license psionic assets or protect Oathbound subjects.
[color=#d9776c]The Militia is restricted to special midround spawns and is not available as a normal starting faction.[/color]
For detailed chains of command, continue to the [textlink="Faction Glossary" link="Glossary"].
